study.title: Acupuncture Reversible Effects on Altered Default Mode Network of Chronic Migraine Accompanied with Clinical Symptom Relief
study.study_design: Longitudinal pre- and postacupuncture treatment (PPAT) study with healthy control comparison group; resting-state fMRI
study.population: Chronic migraine patients without aura and age- and gender-matched healthy controls
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) CM without aura that fulfilled the International Classification of Headache Disorders III (ICHD-3 beta): headache occurring with a frequency of 15 or more days per month for >3 months, of which at least 8 days had the features of migraine headache; (2) an available, patient-recorded daily diary of headache (including frequency of headache attacks, headache days, amount of acute headache medications, and pain intensity); (3) clinical pain assessment with a VAS score > 4 (range, 0–10); and (4) no acupuncture treatment during the preceding month.
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) participation in another clinical study before acupuncture treatment or overuse of pain medication; (2) any other neurological or psychiatric disorder; (3) pregnancy or lactation; (4) other types of headache; (5) history of head trauma or brain tumor; (6) contraindication for MRI scanning; and (7) use of any preventive medications for migraine.

arms.dropouts: 16 patients excluded during treatment period (failure to complete all treatments and use of other medications); 5 CM patients excluded for ineligible fMRI data
7 HCs excluded for ineligible fMRI data

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: T2*-weighted echo planar image (EPI) sequence for functional images; fast spoil gradient recall sequence for T1-weighted anatomical images
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: resampled voxel size of 3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm; slice thickness = 4 mm, gap = 0 mm (functional); slice thickness = 1 mm (anatomical)
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Data Processing & Analysis for Brain Imaging (DPABI, http://rfmri.org/dpabi) toolbox
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: GIFT software (Group ICA Toolbox, http://mialab.mrn.org/software/gift/) for ICA; DPABI toolbox for SCA
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space using diffeomorphic anatomical registration through exponentiated lie algebra (DARTEL) tool
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: head motion realignment; six head motion parameters removed as nuisance signals

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or placebo control arm was included in this study. The study compared CM patients pre- and post-treatment against healthy controls only. There is no sham condition.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported in this study.
Adverse events are not reported anywhere in the paper.
Deqi/sensory response was mentioned as intended ('to elicit the de qi sensation') but no quantitative measure of deqi or other sensation was reported.

The L_PRECUN MNI coordinates reported in text (Section 3.2) are '0, -54, 18' while Table 1 reports L_PRECUN MNI coordinates as '-6, -54, 18'. These are inconsistent. The text says 'MNI coordinates x, y, and z: 0, -54, and 18' while Table 1 lists x = -6 for L_PRECUN.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 5, Section 3.2 text vs. Page 3, Table 1

extraction_notes.note: The R_SPFG and R_TPL MNI coordinates in Table 1 appear to replicate values from L_SPFG and L_TPL (R_SPFG: x=-21, y=60, z=9; R_TPL: x=-39, y=18, z=-27). These appear to be typographic errors in the original paper as right hemisphere coordinates would typically have positive x values.

The bar graphs in Figure 3 show mean DMN z-scores for HC, Pretreatment, and Posttreatment groups for L_SPFG and L_PRECUN, but exact numerical values are not given in the text or tables - only visual representation in the bar graphs. Statistical significance markers are shown (** and *) but exact p-values for these comparisons are not stated beyond the thresholds.

The pairwise FC matrix plots (Figure 4a-c) show r values but individual numerical r-values for specific edges are only readable from Figure 4(f) for the significant pairs, and not precisely reported in the text. The exact r-values visible in Figure 4(f) are approximate from the bar graphs.
No trial registration number is provided.

The ICA analysis yielded a DMN with specific ROIs listed in Table 1, but the number of total independent components identified and the criteria for selecting the DMN component are only partially described (MDL criteria, GIFT software). The exact component selected is not described in detail.
Practitioner qualifications and experience are not described.

The cluster extent values in Table 1 (e.g., L_SPFG=121, L_PRECUN=168) appear to be from the overall DMN component extent rather than cluster extents for the pretreatment vs. HC contrast specifically. The paper does not clearly distinguish whether Table 1 represents the HC DMN ROIs or the contrast-specific clusters.
The paper does not report how many ICs were identified in total before DMN selection, or the specific IC number assigned to the DMN component.
Global signal regression is not mentioned; only white matter signal and CSF signal regression are described as nuisance regressors.

Figure 4(f) shows bar graphs with significance markers (*, **) for pairwise FC comparisons, but the exact r-values for HC, Pretreatment, and Posttreatment groups per edge are only readable approximately from the figure. These were not extracted as numerical values due to figure-only reporting.
